description: A percent consumes what follows it, and a percent with nothing after it consumes itself. d3 reads the character after the percent — and a pad modifier before it — looks it up, and pushes whatever the table gave back: the character itself where there is no entry, and the empty string where the pattern ended first, `charAt` past the end being the empty string. The bottom axis asks for `%~`, which is no directive at all, and reads `~` with the percent gone; the top asks for `%-~` and reads the same, the modifier swallowed with it; the second bottom axis asks for `%b%` and reads the month alone, its dangling percent dropped; and the left asks for `%-`, a modifier with nothing to pad, which consumes all of itself so every label on it is empty — which is why the modifier is looked for *up to* the last character rather than one short of it. A malformed specifier is not an error anywhere in this: it is read the way d3 reads it, which is the only answer a chart can be compared against. Two axes share the bottom on purpose, that being the shape which first looked like a guide-ordering defect and turned out to be the harvester flattening the whitespace it read.
